Title: No Tradable Monthly Equity Signals After Removing Look-Ahead Analyst Revisions

Abstract:
We evaluate ten stock characteristics for predicting next-month returns in a 60,000-row monthly panel of 1,213 stocks. The only feature with strong rank IC is analyst_rev (mean IC = 0.296, t = 89.6), but its data dictionary timing shows it is recorded at the end of month t+1, making it contemporaneous with ret_next and unavailable at the month-t signal date. All other features have mean rank ICs between -0.004 and +0.006 with |t| < 2, and long-short Sharpe ratios between -0.27 and +0.72. After excluding the look-ahead feature, no characteristic provides robust tradable predictive power. The appropriate strategy is therefore no active signal-based trading.

Methods:
Data: 120 months, 500 stocks/month, 60,000 rows. Features point-in-time at end t except analyst_rev. Target ret_next over t+1. Signal evaluation: Spearman rank IC per month, average across months, t-stat = mean(IC)/std(IC)*sqrt(120). Long-short equal-weighted quintile portfolios. Validity criteria: (1) available at end of month t; (2) |t| > 2; (3) positive economic magnitude after costs. We use provided summary statistics only.

Results:
Table? We'll write in text. analyst_rev: IC 0.2958, t 89.59, LS 8.66% monthly, Sharpe 26.38, 100% months positive. But invalid due to timing. Other features: book_to_market IC -0.0030, t -0.72, LS -0.11% mo, Sharpe -0.27; gross_prof 0.0039, t 0.93, LS 0.10%, Sharpe 0.26; log_mktcap 0.0001, t 0.02, LS 0.03%, Sharpe 0.08; asset_growth 0.0061, t 1.64, LS 0.28%, Sharpe 0.72; accruals 0.0055, t 1.34, LS 0.29%, Sharpe 0.70; idio_vol 0.0043, t 1.14, LS 0.03%, Sharpe 0.08; leverage -0.0043, t -1.00, LS -0.02%, Sharpe -0.05; turnover 0.0001, t 0.02, LS 0.01%, Sharpe 0.02; rd_intensity -0.0002, t -0.05, LS 0.05%, Sharpe 0.13. No non-look-ahead feature has |t| > 2. The largest is asset_growth at t=1.64, which is not significant and likely due to multiple testing. Therefore no valid signals.

Discussion:
The analyst_rev result is a classic look-ahead bias. It is recorded after the return month, so a real-time investor cannot observe it at the time of portfolio formation. Its extreme IC and Sharpe confirm it is not a tradable signal but mechanical. The remaining features are either weak, statistically insignificant, or economically trivial. Some signs align with known anomalies (e.g., book_to_market negative, gross_prof positive, accruals positive contrary to literature), but the magnitudes are small and t-stats low. With 10 features tested, the maximum |t| of 1.64 is consistent with noise. Transaction costs would further erode any weak long-short returns. Thus, the best strategy is to abstain from signal-based trading.

Limitations:
- Only 120 months and 500 stocks/month, limiting statistical power.
- No transaction costs, borrow costs, or market impact considered.
- Equal-weighted quintile portfolios may not be implementable.
- Annual accounting data can be stale up to 12 months.
- No out-of-sample validation or multiple-testing adjustment beyond noting it.
- We cannot test lagged analyst_rev or alternative transformations.
- The universe is index constituents, so results may not generalize to broader markets.
- No risk model or sector neutrality.
